newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The country has 1.7 million users of illegal drugs who consume about 17 billion pesos worth of narcotics every month, Philippine National Police narcotics group head Rex Piad said on Thursday. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Law enforcers are on alert as militant labour and public transport groups stage on Friday a nationwide strike to press government for a legislated wage increase and to roll back the prices of petroleum products. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- The Commission on Elections gave up hope yesterday of holding computerised elections next year, saying even if the law was approved on Friday, it could no longer implement it because of time constraints. (BULLETIN/TIMES)
- Hongkong Bank has seen a net inflow of portfolio investment funds to the Philippines every week since July 11, said Mark Boyne, the bank's senior vice president for treasury. (INQUIRER)

- For the first time since the de facto devaluation of the peso on July 11, the central bank on Friday bought about $35 million from the Philippine Dealing System at the rate of 28.37 to the dollar, central bank governor Gabriel Singson said (BUSINESSWORLD/TIMES)
- The government hopes to raise 8.62 billion pesos next year to partly finance the 1998 budget from two tax measures, one recently passed and the other still pending in Congress. (BUSINESSWORLD)
